name: CHCKX Filament
summary: Amazon-first budget filament label with a WooCommerce storefront at chckx3d.com, spanning PLA and specialty PLA through engineering grades (ABS, PETG, PCTG, TPU, PA6-GF, PP-CF/PP-GF, PPA-CF) at prices three to four times below market for the engineering materials. The about page claims in-house vertically-integrated US production and ISO-certified quality control, but no certificate number, factory, plant photo or legal entity is given, and no TDS or SDS exists for any product. The stated headquarters, 1234 N Spring St, Los Angeles CA 90012, resolves to a residential condo unit per Redfin; the only contact is a personal Gmail address (yinchangfeng86@gmail.com); no social profiles exist; and one product page (PETG) still contains placeholder text reading "Test". The evidence therefore points to a reseller or rebrand of undisclosed third-party OEM production rather than a manufacturer. Independent testing reported in a Prusa community forum thread found two products materially mislabeled: a "PPS-CF" that was ABS-based and a "PPA-CF" that was PA6-CF. The same thread describes PC spools and thermally printed labels that smear. Treat all chemistry claims on this brand as unverified.

oem_relationships.notes: No factory, plant, legal entity or ISO certificate number is disclosed anywhere on the site or in listings. The residential-condo headquarters address, personal Gmail contact, Amazon-first distribution, absence of any TDS/SDS, and engineering-grade pricing three to four times below market are all consistent with rebranded imported spools rather than in-house extrusion. China origin is inferred from the distribution and pricing pattern only; the actual producer is unidentified and the relationship is suspected, not confirmed.

product_lines.name: GF-ABS Filament
product_lines.notes: 10% glass-fiber ABS, $18.99; claimed HDT 100C and flexural modulus 3300 MPa, unsupported by any datasheet. Also appears in the 3dfilamentprofiles Amazon catalog as ABS-GF.

product_lines.name: PETG Filament
product_lines.notes: Standard PETG, $12.00. Product page is unfinished and still contains placeholder body text reading "Test"; no print parameters are published.

product_lines.name: PCTG Blend
product_lines.notes: Amazon-catalog variant listed on 3dfilamentprofiles alongside PCTG Basic; the blend is undescribed, so the base pctg id is used.

product_lines.name: TPU Filament (Shore 98A)
product_lines.notes: 98A, firm end of the 95A-class grade band. From $15.99; listed 210-230C nozzle, unheated bed.

product_lines.name: PP-CF Filament
product_lines.notes: pp-cf — coverage gap, no catalog id yet. Carbon-fiber polypropylene, $19.98; listed 230-280C nozzle, 80-110C bed.

product_lines.name: PPA-CF Filament
product_lines.notes: Sold as 10% carbon-fiber PPA at $22.79 with a claimed HDT of 195C and 280-310C nozzle / 100-120C bed. Chemistry is disputed: independent testing reported in the Prusa forum thread found this product to be PA6-CF, not a polyphthalamide. The ppa-cf id follows the vendor's labeling only and should not be relied on; if the forum finding holds, pa6-cf is the correct chemistry.

additional_notes: Origin is unresolved and manufacturing_countries is deliberately left empty. headquarters_country is set to United States because that is the storefront's claimed base (1234 N Spring St, Los Angeles CA 90012), but Redfin shows that address as a residential condo unit, not an industrial or warehouse site, so it is best read as a mail/registration address rather than a plant. No factory location, corporate entity, ISO certificate number, TDS or SDS was found anywhere, so the country where the filament is actually extruded cannot be asserted in either direction; China is a suspicion recorded under oem_relationships, not a finding. Distribution is primarily Amazon (ASINs B0FLK2KDSX, B0FLK15JP8, B0FLJXQH5D, B0FLK1NRN9), where 3dfilamentprofiles.com catalogs 150+ SKU/color combinations, a range far wider than the 14 SKUs on the company storefront. The Prusa forum thread additionally notes PC spools and thermally printed labels that smear in handling. Build plates: none found, so makes_plates is left unset. All quoted fiber loadings, HDT and modulus figures are vendor marketing claims with no supporting documentation.

provenance.conflicts: Identity is contested. The about page claims in-house, vertically integrated US manufacturing with ISO-certified quality control, but supplies no certificate number, factory, plant imagery or legal entity, and no TDS or SDS exists for any SKU. Against that claim: the stated Los Angeles headquarters resolves to a residential condo unit per Redfin, the only contact is a personal Gmail address, distribution is Amazon-first with a catalog several times larger than the storefront, no social presence exists, and one product page still carries placeholder text. Engineering-grade filaments are priced three to four times below market. The weight of evidence favours a reseller/rebrand of undisclosed third-party OEM production, likely China-based, over the claimed US manufacturer; neither is proven. Product labeling is separately contested: independent testing reported in the Prusa forum thread found a product sold as "PPS-CF" to be ABS-based and the "PPA-CF" to be PA6-CF, so the PPA-CF mapping in product_lines follows vendor labeling that testing contradicts. headquarters_country (claimed storefront base) and manufacturing_countries (left empty) should not be read as verified.
